Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all. We transform diverse data into a unified fabric for health. Our platform delivers actionable insights for our customers to advance care and research, drive strategic growth, and achieve financial success. For more information, visit arcadia.io .

Why This Role Is Important To Arcadia

At Arcadia.io , an Implementation Manager (IM) is a highly capable project leader who does what it takes to successfully deliver our product and is the one person responsible for bringing the customer live. This role is the single nexus of a customer getting value out of Arcadia and Arcadia getting value out of their customer. The IM provides the first interaction and touchpoint throughout the relationship. As a result the IM makes a meaningful contribution to retention and the customer experience.

Implementation Managers have complete responsibility for the end-to-end design, execution, and management of implementation activities. IMs commit to running large, complex implementation projects at high quality and speed to accelerate the path to value for our customers.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, can manage competing priorities, understand data architecture and can communicate effectively with technical functions, client, business and clinical teams.

What Success Looks Like

In 3 months

Learn about our platform, industry, and internal processes; complete onboarding requirements and Arcadia Core Platform Certification Engage with leading customers, participating in the development and execution of complex implementation plans and supporting client discussions and working sessions around implementation initiatives
Manage components of the implementation such as integration workstreams

In 6 months

Get to know the ins and outs of our technical implementation process; demonstrate knowledge of client data and platform configuration
Independently manage multiple components of the implementation, including data integration and module implementations

In 12 months

Independently manage an implementation from contract signature to go live, including all aspects of developing an implementation plan, managing project status, handling risks and issues, and coordinating across teams to deliver a successful implementation of our platform
Obtain advanced certification on at least 1 additional module, demonstrating your knowledge of industry context, product functionality, and implementation best practices
Contribute to implementation process improvement initiatives, defining best practices and improving tools and documentation

What You'll Be Doing

Running product implementations, developing project plan and coordinating kickoff, product installation, validation, training, and go live

Escalating and leading resolution of risks and issues including understanding complex technical challenges. Designing custom solutions leveraging Arcadia’s products and service capabilities
Responsible for customer communications. Owning all standing and ad-hoc project meetings
Coordinating customer, internal, and third-party activities. Ensuring project team collaboration and early escalation if project is tracking behind
Demonstrating strong organizational, presentation, and customer service skills; Communicating effectively on data structures and platform architecture
Clearly communicating program/project status, issues, risks, plans, etc. to senior management

Bachelor’s degree in related field
At least 3 years leading account implementation processes in the software or technology arena in healthcare, preferably with claims and clinical data integration; in depth knowledge of and up to date hands-on experience with project management principles, tools and methods; ability to identify and effectively mitigate project- and account-level risks
Extensive healthcare experience, including industry knowledge of population health and value-based care required, including ability to master an in-depth understanding of our solutions, client strategic context, and industry trends to effectively advise clients as a trusted advisor in leveraging the data asset and platform
Experience with data aggregation and analysis with EHR and claims data strongly preferred, including experience with Tableau, QlikView, and SQL

Excellent presentation and communication skills, including ability to create powerful materials in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Word, etc. Must have the ability to lead successful client meetings with executive, operational, clinical, and technical stakeholders
Strong problem solving, interpersonal, and organizational skills
Team attitude and the ability to foster team atmosphere within each project team; ability to work effectively with remote teams

What You'll Get

Be a part of a mission driven company that is transforming the healthcare industry by changing the way patients receive care
A flexible, remote friendly company with personality and heart
Employee driven programs and initiatives for personal and professional development
Be a member of the Arcadian and Barkadian Community

3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions.

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About The Role

As an Implementation Project Manager at 3E, you’ll lead larger, more complex customer implementations where successful delivery requires multiple products, technical contributors, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders to operate against one coordinated plan.

You’ll be accountable for turning the customer’s scope of work into an executable implementation strategy and for determining whether the overall project succeeds—on time, within scope, adopted, and connected to a clear customer outcome. You’ll establish success and acceptance criteria, own the integrated project plan, manage risk and change, coordinate specialists and technical teams, and give both customers and 3E leadership a clear, data-backed view of project health.

You’ll understand the technical delivery deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify dependencies, connect customer needs with the right specialists, and engage credibly with Product and Engineering. You won’t need to personally execute every configuration, migration, or integration; your role is to ensure those pieces come together into a successful customer outcome.

What You’ll Do

Lead complex new-logo, cross-sell, and Value Realization implementations from internal handoff through customer acceptance and formal close.
Translate complex scopes of work into an integrated delivery strategy covering products, workstreams, milestones, resources, dependencies, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria.

Own the master implementation plan and coordinate implementation specialists, Product, Engineering, Data, Cloud, technical consultants, external partners, and customer resources.
Establish measurable success and acceptance criteria at kickoff and maintain accountability for those outcomes throughout delivery.
Lead customer project governance, including senior stakeholder and sponsor communications.
Maintain the milestone tracker and conduct phase-gate reviews, giving a clear assessment of whether projects are on track, at risk, or behind and establishing mitigation plans when required.
Identify cross-workstream dependencies and risks early and determine their impact on the critical path.
Lead complex, multi-product delivery by managing scope and change control, coordinating custom development through launch, maintaining a unified customer plan across teams, and providing leadership with clear, data-backed reporting on project health, risk, timelines, value, and adoption.
Build and maintain dashboards or reporting tools that make project status and risks visible without relying solely on status meetings.
Lead customer escalations diplomatically while maintaining accountability for customer commitments, decisions, resources, data readiness, and signoffs.

But delivery is only part of your legacy here. Your field experience becomes the playbook for the next generation of delivery leaders. Champion AspireHR's interests — protect scope, enforce methodology, and push back when needed to safeguard the team
Elevate the PM practice by contributing lessons learned, delivery insights, and best practices to AspireHR's internal knowledge bases, tools, and methodology frameworks

Demonstrates understanding of the integration points with other HR systems and modules

Laurel is on a mission to return time. As the leading AI Time platform for professional services firms, we’re transforming how organizations capture, analyze, and optimize their most valuable resource: time. Our proprietary machine learning technology automates work time capture and connects time data to business outcomes, enabling firms to increase profitability, improve client delivery, and make data-driven strategic decisions. We serve many of the world's largest accounting and law firms, including EY, Aprio, Crowell & Moring, and Frost Brown Todd, and process over 1 billion work activities annually that have never been collected and aggregated before Laurel’s AI Time platform.

Our team comprises top talent in AI, product development, and engineering—innovative, humble, and forward-thinking professionals committed to redefining productivity in the knowledge economy. We're building solutions that empower workers to deliver twice the value in half the time, giving people more time to be creative and impactful. If you're passionate about transforming how people work and building a lasting company that explores the essence of time itself, we'd love to meet you.

About The Role:

We're looking for a Senior Technical Project Manager
to own the end-to-end onboarding and implementation journey for new enterprise customers. You'll sit at the center of every new deployment — orchestrating the work between customers and Laurel's implementation engineers, keeping projects on track, and ensuring every go-live is high quality, not just on time.

This role is for someone who is equally comfortable in a kickoff call with a customer's executive team and a technical deep-dive with an engineer. You translate complexity into clarity, manage competing priorities without losing momentum, and treat Time to Value as a guiding metric — never at the expense of the customer experience.

What You Will Do:

Lead end-to-end onboarding and implementation projects from signed contract through go-live and CSM handoff.
Orchestrate deployment of the Laurel tenant and Boomi Atom in coordination with implementation engineers.
Guide customers through technical integration setup for Microsoft Office, Email, Phone, Video Conferencing, and SSO.
Run kickoff calls and host ongoing office hours for end users and finance teams throughout the implementation lifecycle.
Triage issues in real time — escalating to engineering or leadership appropriately while maintaining customer confidence.
Coordinate with CSMs on adoption strategies and active user growth as customers move through and beyond go-live.
Maintain clear project plans, timelines, and milestone tracking across multiple concurrent accounts using tools like Asana and Microsoft Planner.
Translate technical concepts — integration architecture, XPATH-based mapping, API behaviors — into clear language for stakeholders at all levels.
Apply agentic AI tools and technology-enabled workflows to scale your own effectiveness and bring creative efficiency to implementation challenges.

What We're Looking For:

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Strategic Management, Management Information Systems, Computer Information Systems, or a related field.
5+ years of project management experience delivering complex technical implementations in a B2B SaaS environment.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent customer engagements without sacrificing quality or responsiveness.
Proficiency with project management tools such as Asana, Microsoft Planner, or comparable platforms; strong task-oriented design instincts.
Technical aptitude to work directly with engineers — experience with Boomi, XPATH, or enterprise integration platforms is a strong plus.
Familiarity with enterprise tech stacks: Microsoft 365, SSO protocols (SAML/OAuth), email, calendar, phone, and video conferencing systems.
Working knowledge of or strong curiosity about agentic AI tools and process automation — you use these tools, not just know of them.
Excellent communicator across all settings: executive briefings, customer calls, written updates, and engineering stand-ups.
PMP, CAPM, or equivalent certification is a plus.

What Laurel is

Laurel is building the system of record for human and agentic work.

The trust Laurel has built with regulated enterprises—and, even more importantly, their end-users— has enabled it to be the first company ever to deploy a multimodal desktop agent at scale (45K+ professionals and 70+ countries). This enables Laurel to collect work that no one else has.

Half of enterprise work happens in systems with no API or OS-level access which no tech—other than a multimodal desktop agent—can capture.

Laurel collects more than just metadata; it captures the work itself. And to make the data useful, Laurel builds workflows that requires the professional who did the work to label it accurately, creating a reinforcement learning flywheel that nobody else in the world has.

The result is +2B (and counting) of human-verified labels, creating what is becoming the world’s largest repository of last-mile enterprise data and workflows.

How Laurel did it

Laurel developed its data infrastructure by creating the AI Billing category in professional services (legal, accounting, consulting). Laurel earned the trust of the enterprise (in the form of +$1B in profit returned) and end-users (in the form of 1.53M work hours returned) to collect all digital work, even work happening in digital systems that were previously invisible to AI.

Laurel is now re-running the same playbook in financial services (insurance, banks, private equity, etc). Same data infrastructure. But instead of billing, it is creating the Work Observability category to expand its feedback loop.

What’s next

Packaging its last-mile data in the form of:

Post-training: an open-source model on Laurel’s data improved performance by 33%, matching the frontier, at 1% of the cost.
Context: Feeding this data into a frontier model’s context window improves task automation by 21%.
This is how Laurel accelerates its growth from 4x YoY (current) to +10x YoY).

jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

The Global Learning & Development (GL&D) Measurement Lead drives operational and business-impact measurement capabilities across GL&D by helping teams build meaningful measurement plans and translating data into insights that improve decisions and demonstrate value to the business.

As GL&D evolves from measuring learning activity to demonstrating business value, this role serves as the department's authority on learning effectiveness, business impact, strategic performance, and operational reporting. The Measurement Lead establishes consistent frameworks and standards while helping teams connect learning investments, strategic priorities, and operational performance to measurable outcomes.

This role operates in close partnership with the GL&D Strategy Lead and Strategy Execution and Change Management Lead, as well as HR analytics and reporting teams. Success is measured by the quality, consistency, and use of measurement across GL&D and by the extent to which insights improve decisions, strengthen execution, and demonstrate value to the business.

Key Responsibilities

GL&D Measurement & Performance Reporting

Own the GL&D Success Scorecard, transformation metrics, portfolio health reporting, and Quarterly Business Review measurement packages as the department's single source of truth.
Develop and maintain department measurement frameworks, KPI standards, scorecard templates, definitions, and reporting methodologies that create consistency across GL&D.
Translate performance data into clear executive insights, business stories, and recommendations that support prioritization and decision-making.

Measurement Consulting & Strategic Partnership

Consult with learning teams and program managers to identify success criteria, business metrics data sources, outcome measures, data ownership, measurement plans, review processes, and practical evaluation approaches based on defined business needs.
Partner with the Strategy Lead and Strategy Execution and Change Management Lead to define success measures, benefits-realization plans, baselines, targets, and reporting approaches for strategic priorities and major transformation initiatives.
Partner with learning teams and the strategy team to interpret findings, identify root causes, and recommend actions based on data insights.
Partner with the HR analytics team on business impact analysis projects.
Balance analytical rigor with data availability, decision needs, and practical business constraints to create measurement approaches that teams can execute and sustain.

Reporting Requirements & Measurement Capability

Define user stories, business requirements, measure definitions, acceptance criteria, and reporting needs for dashboards and performance reporting, and partner with HR analytics and reporting teams to execute.
Build measurement capability across GL&D through coaching, office hours, templates, job aids, manager resources, and Learning Consultant development.
Continuously improve measurement practices, standards, tools, and reporting approaches to strengthen GL&D's ability to demonstrate value and impact.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
Eight to ten years of experience in project management activities

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing measurement strategies, performance frameworks, scorecards, dashboards, or business-impact reporting in a learning, HR, strategy, analytics, or enterprise environment.
Ability to connect learning investments, operational performance, and strategic initiatives to measurable business outcomes and benefits realization.
Strong analytical and data-literacy skills, including the ability to define meaningful measures, interpret quantitative and qualitative data, identify patterns, and develop evidence-based recommendations.
Experience translating business needs into user stories, reporting requirements, measure definitions, and acceptance criteria for analytics and reporting teams.
Excellent communication, consultation, influence, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to simplify complex information and build stronger measurement practices without direct authority.
Strong business acumen and judgment, with the ability to balance analytical rigor, data limitations, stakeholder needs, and practical execution.
Background in Learning & Development, learning analytics, people analytics, business intelligence, program evaluation, organizational effectiveness, or a related field.
Experience with learning evaluation and impact methodologies, such as the Kirkpatrick Model, Phillips ROI Methodology, logic models, or benefits-realization practices.
Experience developing executive scorecards, portfolio health reporting, Quarterly Business Review packages, or transformation-performance reporting.
Familiarity with business intelligence and reporting platforms such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent enterprise analytics tools.
Experience partnering with data, analytics, technology, or reporting teams to design and deliver dashboards and recurring performance reporting.
Knowledge of data governance, KPI documentation, reporting controls, data quality, and responsible interpretation of performance measures.

jobs.title: Senior Identity Intelligence / Counterintelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
Purpose and Impact:

Our industry-leading intelligence support program informs decision-makers, from ground force commanders to international partners and national security policymakers. Our employees lead the Intelligence community in providing superior Identity Intelligence and regional threat analysis, and developing innovative data-driven solutions, supporting the customer through intelligence analysis and tradecraft proliferation.

Work Schedule:
5 days per week, 8 hours per day

Essential Responsibilities:

As an Identity Intelligence / Counterintelligence Analyst, you will be responsible for producing all-source Identity Intelligence (I2) analysis and intelligence products in support of global missions and customers. You will apply an understanding of I2 and targeting tradecraft to produce analysis focused on the full range of unique identifying human characteristics and modalities to include, but not limited to, fingerprints, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), iris scans, voiceprints, facial recognition features, and behavior for the purposes of identifying and tracking persons and networks. This includes fusing identity attributes, such as biographical, biological, behavioral, contextual, and reputational information related to individuals and intelligence associated with those attributes, to identify and assess threats of individuals and networks, their capabilities and capacity, centers of gravity, objectives, intent, and potential courses of action.

Work Environment, Physical Demands, and Mental Demands:
Typical office environment with no unusual hazards, constant sitting while using the computer terminal, constant use of sight abilities while reviewing documents, constant use of speech/hearing abilities for communication and constant mental alertness. Must possess planning/organizing skills and must be able to work under deadlines.

Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities):

Possesses an extensive knowledge of applicable databases; ability to compile, analyze and synthesize necessary data to provide an assessment within the scope of the assigned mission and government approved format.
Expertise in and demonstrated ability to apply IC and DoD classification guidelines and procedures.
Extensive experience with I2 analytical tools and databases, including BI2R/I2AR, SOFEX, Palantir, AIDP/Maven, Query Tree, Chrome, Analyst Notebook, Open-Source research, Biometric Automated Toolset (BAT), TIDE, Pulse, QLIX.
Demonstrates mastery of qualitative and quantitative analytic methodologies and pursue developments in academia or other fields that affect tradecraft methodology. Demonstrates ability to define comprehensive, new, or unique research approaches that enable rigorous assessments to address and contribute to high-level tasks.
Demonstrates ability to conduct in-depth analysis of analytic operations and knowledge management issues across organizational and intra-IC boundaries and clearly articulates key findings.
Demonstrates ability to work independently and with minimal to no oversight.
Demonstrated ability to review analytic products for cogent arguments, tradecraft standards, and adequate support for conclusions; routinely tests analytic rigor of analytic products.

Security Clearance Required:

TS/SCI

Minimum Education:

High School Education

Minimum Years of Experience:

14 yrs relevant experience, 10 yrs w/ Bachelor’s Degree

jobs.title: Disaster Management & Humanitarian Assistance Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview

The Disaster Management & Humanitarian Assistance Research Analyst supports the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance (CFE-DM) within the Applied Research and Information Sharing (ARIS) program. This position conducts academic research, analysis, and technical writing focused on disaster management and humanitarian assistance, developing operationally relevant publications that strengthen understanding, coordination, and effectiveness across disaster response and humanitarian assistance missions.

The Research Analyst researches and synthesizes complex information to produce high-quality academic and technical products addressing disaster management capabilities, vulnerabilities, and best practices around the world, with particular emphasis on the Pacific Theater. The position requires strong academic research methodologies, advanced writing and editing capabilities, and the ability to translate research findings into practical recommendations for civil-military coordination and humanitarian assistance operations.

Working with subject matter experts, academic institutions, international organizations, and CFE-DM personnel, the Research Analyst contributes to publications, country studies, case studies, training materials, and other information-sharing products that support the Center's mission.

Responsibilities

Academic Research and Technical Writing

Conduct research, analysis, and synthesis of disaster management data and information to produce accurate, comprehensive publications aligned with client-specific style and content requirements, including international civil-military coordination contexts.
Develop a wide range of disaster management and humanitarian assistance materials, including:
Fact sheets, case studies, best practices, research articles, and research studies.
Disaster management reference country handbooks.
Briefings, presentations, memoranda, information and policy papers, planning documents, and conference materials.
Professional journal publications, situation reports, after-action reports, and time-sensitive requests for information (RFIs).

Apply academic research methodologies to identify, evaluate, and communicate relevant findings.
Translate research findings into operationally relevant information and practical recommendations for disaster management and humanitarian assistance stakeholders.

Case Study Development and Training Support

Design and develop operationally relevant disaster response case studies for use in training modules.
Support civil-military training, exercises, operations, short- and long-term planning, and assessments in alignment with the applicable theater campaign plan through research, information sharing, and the exchange of best practices.

Collaboration, Editing, and Quality Assurance

Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to collect and validate information, verify data integrity, and ensure analytic accuracy.
Facilitate integration of external feedback into documents by reviewing comments, recommending improvements, and ensuring products meet target audience needs.
Edit research products for logical flow, clarity, completeness, grammar, punctuation, and overall content quality.
Coordinate with graphics and design staff to ensure drafts meet final production standards for web and print publication.
Directly support print production and inventory management of information products.

Academic Partnerships, Outreach, and Knowledge Sharing

Support the Academic Partnership Program by cultivating academic partnerships and facilitating information exchange with universities, students and interns, academic partners, international organizations, and related networks.
Update data management and information-sharing plans to support program operations.
Coordinate marketing and outreach activities as needed, including website updates, brochure and report development, social media and newsletter content, and engagement with external institutions.
Provide guidance to students on research papers and edit or revise academic papers to translate findings into practical DMHA recommendations.
Coordinate with CFE staff to ensure students are fully integrated and resourced.
Respond to academic inquiries and curate strategic research topics to provide project options for incoming students.

Stakeholder Engagement, Program Operations, and Events

Liaise with other CFE-DM branches and engage staff with relevant expertise, relationships, or country and subject matter knowledge.
Organize and facilitate events, training sessions, and exercises tied to product development and dissemination.
Prepare and deliver presentations and briefings at CFE academic engagements, workshops, and exercises.
Attend regular CFE-DM and PACOM meetings and maintain an updated task and deliverables dashboard for CFE-DM and ARIS.
Support event setup, unpack boxes of information products, and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Master's degree required. Bachelor's and/or Master's degree in English, Communications, Journalism/Public Affairs, International Studies, Disaster Management, or a related field.
Minimum five years of experience analyzing and synthesizing information, including writing and editing disaster research products.
Strong academic research, writing, and editing capabilities, with the ability to understand and accurately communicate DMHA content in Standard U.S. English.
Experience developing research products and technical publications addressing disaster management, humanitarian assistance, or related subject areas.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present reports, briefings, and presentations.
Ability to prioritize multiple concurrent tasks, manage shifting timelines, and maintain strong time management and delivery discipline.
Advanced Microsoft Word skills, including formatting, editing, and publishing technical reports and similar products.
Ability to take direction while operating independently with a high degree of autonomy, along with strong collaboration skills and respect for diverse perspectives.
Experience developing products that promote civil-military coordination during humanitarian assistance and disaster response missions and training.
Experience with public speaking, facilitation, and presenting to varied audiences.
U.S. citizenship required.
Must be able to obtain a SECRET security clearance. Sponsorship is available.

Preferred Qualifications

Current SECRET security clearance.
Extensive experience working in higher education research environments and applying academic research methodologies.
Demonstrated experience producing technical academic publications, including published articles addressing disaster management, humanitarian assistance, or humanitarian assistance and disaster response (HADR).
Extensive regional expertise in the Pacific Theater and familiarity with its disaster management and humanitarian assistance environment.

P hysical Requirements:
The ideal candidate must at a minimum be able to meet the following physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation:

Ability to perform repetitive motions with the hands, wrists, and fingers.
Ability to engage in and follow audible communications in emergency situations.
Ability to sit for prolonged periods at a desk and working on a computer.

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

Within the Ministry of Education and Childcare , the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Division provides leadership and strategic direction to support the education system in improving outcomes and creating opportunities for Indigenous students in Alberta. The division collaborates with Indigenous Peoples and other educational partners to understand and respond to the unique academic and cultural needs of Indigenous students and works to ensure Alberta Education programs and policies are responsive, culturally relevant and effective. The Research and Analysis unit, within the Partnerships and Research Branch, provides research, policy analysis, coordination and support relating to policy, research and data functions in support of the division and the Ministry's goals and priorities for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students.

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Manager, Research and Analysis, the Policy and Research Analyst provides research, policy analysis, data analysis, coordination and support relating to policy, research and data functions within the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Division and on cross-ministry projects in which the division is participating. The position supports the advancement of the Ministry's goals and priorities for Indigenous education and for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students, including policies and programs, and works with others in the division and the ministry when needed.

In this role, you will focus on the following main responsibilities:

Research and data analysis: Performs research, jurisdictional scans and literature reviews on assigned topics, analysis of qualitative and quantitative data from reports, databases, grant programs to address key questions, identify trends, promising practices and inform recommendations for Indigenous education policy and initiatives in Alberta.
Policy and program support and coordination: Develops briefings, policy documents, tools and resources, prepares responses to Action Requests, proactively identifies policy gaps and opportunities, and supports the coordination of First Nations, Métis and Inuit education initiatives and grants and other projects across the division and across the ministry.
Relationship building and partner collaboration: Builds and maintains authentic relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit governments, communities and education partners, and collaborates to implement programs and initiatives that help support student success.
Cross-ministry collaboration and project support: Liaises and engages with staff in the branch, division, ministry and across government, and manages multiple projects with varying timelines to support high-level decision making within the department.
Data stewardship and governance: Supports effective data stewardship and governance, acting as a steward for First Nations, Métis and Inuit student-related data in collaboration with ministry partners.

Develop Networks: Maintains close relations with internal and external stakeholders by identifying key relationships, engaging a range of interested parties, and influencing others through effective communication.
Build Collaborative Environments: Facilitates open communication and leverages the skills and knowledge of others, valuing diverse perspectives and supporting respectful conflict resolution.
Systems Thinking: Considers interrelationships and emerging trends to attain goals, analyzing long-term outcomes and anticipating unintended consequences.
Agility: Works effectively in a changing environment, takes initiative to improve work processes, and remains calm and composed in stressful situations.

jobs.description:
Overview

At Community Financial System, Inc. (CFSI), we are dedicated to providing our customers with friendly, personalized, high-quality financial services and products. Our retail division, Community Bank, N.A., operates more than 200 customer facilities across Upstate New York, Northeastern Pennsylvania, Vermont and Western Massachusetts. Beyond retail banking, we also offer commercial banking, wealth management, investment management, insurance and risk management, and benefit plan administration.

Just as our employees are committed to helping our customers manage their finances, we’re committed to our employees. After all, they make it happen for our customers every day.

To ensure our people can enjoy long and successful careers here at CFSI, we offer competitive compensation, great benefits, and professional development and advancement opportunities. As an equal-opportunity workplace and affirmative-action employer, we celebrate and support a diverse workplace for the benefit of all: our employees, customers and communities.

Responsibilities

Direct and manage the day-to-day operations, technical defense capabilities, and personnel of the Information Security department. Exercise full managerial authority over departmental personnel, driving staffing strategy, talent recruitment, coaching, performance evaluation, professional development, succession planning, and accountability for results. Partner with Information Technology to embed Security-by-Design and Zero Trust controls across enterprise systems while applying a risk-based approach to evaluate business initiatives, third-party vendor relationships, and emerging technology/AI integrations. Serve as the operational deputy and designated successor to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), actively participating on the Core Incident Response Team, supporting regulatory examination and audit readiness, and holding full delegated authority to lead departmental operations, personnel, and governance functions in the CISO's absence.

Essential Responsibilities:

Program Governance & CISO Deputization:

Assist the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) in designing, maintaining, and enforcing enterprise Information Security policies, standards, and guidelines aligned with industry frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS Controls, FFIEC).
Serve as operational deputy to the CISO, holding delegated authority to represent the department in IT architecture reviews, change management, and applicable risk and IT committees during the CISO’s absence.

Team Leadership & Security Operations:

Supervise, mentor, and direct daily operations for departmental staff, including Information Security and GRC Analysts.
Oversee real-time security monitoring, ensuring prompt triage, investigation, and escalation of security alerts, anomalous activity, and privileged access events.

Incident Response & Digital Forensics:

Serve as an active core member of the enterprise Incident Response (IR) Team, supporting the CISO in managing security incidents, containment strategies, digital forensics, and root-cause analysis.
Step in as primary Incident Coordinator when the CISO is unavailable.
Coordinate and facilitate recurring tabletop exercises across business and operational units to validate incident readiness.

Cyber-Fraud Fusion & Threat Intelligence:

Actively participate in and support the enterprise Fusion initiative, establishing collaborative workflows, joint threat monitoring, and bi-directional intelligence sharing between Information Security and Fraud Operations.
Oversee the threat intelligence and vulnerability management lifecycle, analyzing cyber-enabled financial fraud tactics, threat actor behaviors, and emerging attack vectors to strengthen preventative controls across banking platforms and digital channels.

Regulatory Examinations & Audit Management:

Serve as an operational coordinator for Internal Audit, external third-party assessors, and banking regulatory examinations (e.g., OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve).
Manage evidence collection, track audit findings and remediation plans, and ensure timely resolution of all internal and external audit commitments.

Vulnerability Lifecycle & Attack Surface Management:

Direct regular vulnerability scans, penetration tests, and attack surface assessments across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud infrastructure, collaborating with IT system owners to prioritize and verify technical remediation.

Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) & AI Governance:

Participate in the enterprise Third-Party Risk Management program, providing guidance and oversight to the department on vendor risk evaluations, SOC reviews, and high-risk security findings.
Participate in the AI Governance Committee to evaluate security risks associated with third-party AI integrations and internal AI/agent solutions in alignment with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

Security Architecture, Cloud & Data Protection:

Direct data protection initiatives (DLP, data discovery/classification, encryption) and cloud security posture assessments across hybrid and cloud environments (e.g., Azure, M365).
Collaborate with IT to enforce Security-by-Design, Threat Modeling, and Least Privilege principles within the change management process and system rollout lifecycle.

Security Tooling Optimization & Administration:

Direct the administration, tuning, and lifecycle management of key defensive tooling, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR), User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA), email security, and Web Application Firewalls (WAF).
Evaluate and pilot emerging defensive technologies to continuously strengthen organizational cyber resilience.

Security Awareness & Culture:

Oversee the enterprise security awareness training and simulated phishing program, analyzing risk trends and deploying targeted education for high-risk roles.

Executive Reporting & Departmental Metrics:

Lead cross-functional cybersecurity initiatives from planning through implementation, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives, regulatory expectations, and risk appetite.
Develop, monitor, and report Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and operational program status to the CISO and risk oversight committees.
Perform other specialized supervisory, threat defense, and risk management duties as assigned by executive leadership.

Ancillary Duties:

As an integral member of the Information Security department, this position is also responsible to provide assistance wherever necessary to help the department and the company in achieving their goals.

Qualifications

Education, Training and Requirements:

Required: Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or equivalent experience.
Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CRISC, or CISA strongly preferred

Skills:

Proven leadership, supervisory, and mentorship capabilities with the ability to manage technical personnel and foster a collaborative team environment.
Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate cybersecurity concepts and risk metrics effectively to technical teams, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
In-depth knowledge of modern enterprise network security, cloud environments, and identity architectures (IAM/PAM, Least Privilege, Zero Trust).
Practical expertise in incident response coordination, digital forensics principles, vulnerability management, and threat intelligence lifecycle management.
Strong working knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS Controls, NIST AI RMF), third-party risk management (TPRM), and financial industry regulatory standards (OCC, FFIEC, GLBA, SOX).

Experience:

7+ years of experience in Information Security and Cybersecurity operations/engineering; OR
8+ years of progressive IT experience with 5+ years dedicated to Information Security, GRC, and Cyber Risk Management.
Proven supervisory/leadership experience managing security staff and programs.
Financial industry experience (familiarity with FFIEC, OCC, FDIC, GLBA, SOX) strongly preferred.
Experience with Cloud Security (Azure/M365), modern IAM/PAM, and emerging risk frameworks (such as AI Governance / NIST AI RMF).
All applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

jobs.title: Regional Sustainment Framework (RSF) Program Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview

The Regional Sustainment Framework (RSF) Program Analyst provides logistics planning, operational coordination, and strategic analysis support to the PACOM Logistics and Engineering Directorate (J4) in operationalizing the Regional Sustainment Framework. Assigned to the Multinational Logistics Branch, Plans & Exercise Division (J45), this position focuses on optimizing theater-level maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities, strengthening bilateral and multilateral logistics partnerships, and integrating logistics posture into the broader Theater Campaign Plan (TCP), Theater Posture Plan (TPP), and Theater Security Cooperation Program (TSCP).

The RSF Program Analyst supports theater sustainment resiliency objectives and operates independently with minimal guidance in a dynamic joint environment. The position conducts high-level logistics capability assessments, facilitates partner engagements, drafts bilateral agreements, and integrates regional MRO initiatives into major joint operations, security cooperation activities, and applicable theater defense plans.

Success requires exceptional written and oral communication skills and the ability to collaborate across multi-echelon Joint Logistics Enterprise (JLEnt) organizations and foreign military counterparts.

Responsibilities

Regional Sustainment Framework Implementation and Strategy

Operationalize the Regional Sustainment Framework strategy within the PACOM area of responsibility (AOR).
Identify, assess, and leverage regional, bilateral, and multilateral maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities to build forward-deployed sustainment resilience.
Conduct high-level logistics capability assessments to identify regional sustainment opportunities and requirements.
Integrate regional MRO initiatives into major joint operations, security cooperation activities, and applicable theater defense plans.

Bilateral and Multilateral Engagements

Plan, coordinate, and execute bilateral logistics staff talks, working groups, and forums with regional allies and key partners, including Australia, Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, and Singapore.
Support the drafting, negotiation, and maintenance of bilateral logistics instruments, including Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreements (ACSA), Memoranda of Understanding or Agreement (MOU/MOA), and Implementing Arrangements (IA).
Facilitate partner engagements and information exchange with foreign military counterparts.

Security Cooperation Integration

Align regional sustainment initiatives with the PACOM Theater Security Cooperation Program.
Coordinate logistics capacity-building projects, Excess Defense Articles (EDA) transfers, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) sustainment to ensure long-term partner-nation interoperability and maintenance self-sufficiency.

Doctrine and Policy Alignment

Ensure regional sustainment plans, bilateral arrangements, and security cooperation activities comply with applicable Department of War Directives and Instructions, Joint Publications, and statutory authorities under Title 10, U.S. Code.
Apply applicable policy and statutory authorities governing theater sustainment, bilateral logistics, and security cooperation activities.

Interagency and Component Coordination

Synchronize RSF and bilateral initiatives across PACOM Service Components, including USARPAC, PACFLT, PACAF, and MARFORPAC.
Coordinate with sub-unified commands, including USFK, USFJ, SOCPAC, and SPACE-PAC.
Coordinate with the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSW(A&S)), Joint Staff J4, and defense agencies, including DLA and DSCA.
Collaborate across multi-echelon Joint Logistics Enterprise organizations and foreign military counterparts.

Executive Reporting and Briefings

Draft high-quality staff products, including Executive Summaries (EXSUMs), Information Papers, Action Memoranda, and Talking Points.
Prepare formal staff packages, action memoranda, bilateral agreements, and background papers.
Deliver executive-level briefings to General and Flag Officers (GO/FO) and foreign defense dignitaries.
Present complex sustainment concepts and recommendations to senior leadership and international defense officials.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
Exceptional written and oral communication skills, including the ability to draft formal staff packages, action memoranda, bilateral agreements, and background papers and present complex sustainment concepts to senior leadership and international defense officials.
Minimum five years of experience operating within a Geographic Combatant Command (GCC) environment, preferably PACOM, or at a sub-unified or Service Component headquarters level.
Demonstrated experience managing bilateral logistics portfolios, participating in bilateral military staff talks, or executing Security Cooperation or Security Assistance programs, such as ACSA, FMS, or Cooperative Logistics Supply Support Arrangements.
Demonstrated understanding of the defense industrial base, product support strategies, depot-level maintenance processes, and global commercial MRO networks.
Proficiency with and ability to apply security cooperation management tools, including Global Theater Security Cooperation Management Information System (G-TSCMIS) / Socium, and logistics databases, including ACSA Global Automated Tracking and Reporting System (AGATRS).
Experience using Tasker Management Systems, including ETMS2, LOGCOP, and AI tools such as Claude and Maven Smart System, as well as other essential information technology systems.
Active SECRET security clearance.
Ability to travel internationally within the PACOM AOR, including Japan, South Korea, Australia, the Philippines, and Singapore, and domestically approximately 6–8 times annually, not to exceed 20%.

Preferred Qualifications

TS/SCI eligibility.

Ability to perform repetitive motions with the hands, wrists, and fingers.
Ability to engage in and follow audible communications in emergency situations.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. The whole-of-nation effort to safely and securely deliver the cutting edge nuclear-powered submarine program will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.

This unique opportunity will see you directly contributing to Australia’s strategic Defence outcomes during an important time in our defence history. The Australian Submarine Agency (ASA) Virginia Program Office (VPO) supports the delivery of critical projects under the Nuclear Powered Submarine Program by providing strategic advice to ensure the compliant acquisition of critical aspects of Australia’s sovereign nuclear powered submarine capability.
The VPO is central to maintain ASA’s relationships with AUKUS Partners through the development and management of Australia’s most critical Foreign Military Sales (FMS) cases and naval nuclear reactor arrangements.

As an APS 6 Project Manager within the Foreign Acquisitions & Export Control Team in the VPO, you will contribute directly to Australia's defence capability outcomes by managing international arrangements, foreign acquisitions, including Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programs, and export control compliance requirements in support of strategic capability delivery.

The Foreign Acquisitions & Export Control Team supports ASA’s delivery of the Optimal Pathway by enabling critical acquisitions, managing strategic risk, and ensuring compliance with export control and government-to-government arrangements.

providing export control policy and regulatory advice

new_jobs.title: Project Manager, Manhattan Active WMS
new_jobs.description:
Be Part of enVista’s Next Chapter

enVista is the leading global supply chain consulting and automation firm, helping organizations optimize supply chain and distribution operations from strategy through execution. With 25+ years of experience serving thousands of leading brands, enVista combines deep expertise across supply chain strategy, digital transformation, and distribution center optimization to design, build, implement and optimize high-performing operations within the four walls and across the broader supply chain.

We are seeking an experienced Project Manager with expertise in Manhattan Associates Active Warehouse Management System (WMS) and a proven track record in successfully implementing WMS solutions. The ideal candidate will possess exceptional project management skills, strong technical knowledge of WMS platforms, and the ability to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver projects on time and within budget.

This is more than just a consulting role, it’s an opportunity to be a thought leader and change-maker at a pivotal time in enVista’s journey. We are investing in our people, systems, and future, and we’re looking for bold innovators who want to build with us.

Why enVista?

Our associates help organizations solve complex supply chain challenges and optimize operations from strategy through execution. We support our people with comprehensive onboarding and training, award, and recognition programs, volunteer and affinity groups, and a strong mentoring culture. We are committed to growing top talent and giving our associates the tools to thrive.

If you’re ready to step into a high-impact role with a company that’s growing, innovating, and leading the market, this is your opportunity.

Apply today and be part of enVista’s next chapter.

What You Will Do

WMS Implementation Planning:
Lead the planning and initiation phase of WMS implementation projects, including scoping, resource allocation, and timeline development.
Collaborate with key stakeholders to define project objectives, deliverables, and success criteria.
Develop a comprehensive project plan, considering dependencies, risks, and contingencies.

Project Monitoring and Control:
Track project progress, identify risks, and proactively address issues to ensure successful project delivery.
Regularly communicate project status, milestones, and risks to stakeholders and executive management.
Monitor project budget, resource utilization, and timelines to ensure adherence to project constraints.

Team Leadership:
Assemble and lead a cross-functional project team, consisting of business analysts, developers, subject matter experts, and other relevant stakeholders.
Provide guidance and support to team members throughout the project lifecycle.
Foster a collaborative and results-oriented work environment.

Requirements Analysis and Solution Design:
Conduct thorough requirements gathering and analysis to understand business needs and align them with WMS capabilities.
Work closely with business users and subject matter experts to define system requirements, workflows, and process improvements.
Collaborate with solution architects and technical teams to design an optimal WMS solution that meets business requirements.

WMS Implementation and Configuration:
Oversee the configuration, customization, and testing of the Manhattan Associates Active WMS platform to align with business processes and requirements.
Manage all aspects of the implementation project, including system configuration, integration with other systems, data migration, and user acceptance testing.
Ensure compliance with project governance, change management processes, and industry best practices.

Application and Integration Testing:
Develop and execute a comprehensive testing strategy for the WMS implementation, including unit testing, system testing, and integration testing.
Collaborate with the development team to ensure that all system components are thoroughly tested and meet functional and performance requirements.
Identify and track defects, working closely with the development team to resolve issues promptly.
Conduct user acceptance testing (UAT) with key stakeholders to validate the system against business requirements and obtain sign-off for implementation.

Training and Documentation:
Develop and execute training plans for end-users, ensuring smooth adoption and effective utilization of the WMS system.
Create comprehensive documentation, including user manuals, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and training materials.

Go-Live Preparation and Readiness:
Lead the go-live preparation activities, ensuring that all necessary components are in place for a successful system launch.
Collaborate with stakeholders to develop a detailed go-live plan, including cutover activities, data migration, and user training.
Coordinate with the IT infrastructure team to ensure the availability and readiness of hardware, networks, and system environments.
Conduct end-to-end testing to validate system functionality and data integrity before go-live.
Develop contingency plans and risk mitigation strategies to address potential issues during the go-live phase.
Provide guidance and support to end-users during the transition period, addressing any concerns or issues that may arise.
Monitor system performance and user feedback post-go-live, making necessary adjustments and enhancements to ensure a smooth operational transition.

What You Will Bring

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (such as Information Systems, Supply Chain Management, or Business Administration) is preferred
5+ years in Supply Chain Consulting
Proven experience as a Project Manager, leading successful Manhattan Associates WMS implementation projects, preferably with Active WMS
Strong understanding of WMS concepts, functionality, and best practices
Excellent project management skills, including project planning, resource allocation, risk management, and stakeholder communication
Ability to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams and drive project deliverables
Solid analytical and problem-solving abilities with keen attention to detail
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Travel expectations up to 50%

Comprehensive Health Coverage– Medical, Dental, and Vision and Prescription coverage, along with HSA/FSA options that work for you and your family
Time to recharge and give back– Flexible paid time off (PTO), holidays and unlimited volunteering days

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Works with management and stakeholders to align priorities and goals using technical know-how in a fundamental engineering area or technical domain. Establishes scope and milestones for each aspect of a technical program, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals. Manages technical programs and complex, cross-organizational initiatives impacting products and business. Manages highly complex issues, bottlenecks and/or risks, escalating issues when appropriate. Leads technical program improvement, implementing best practices and driving cross-team process optimizations to improve processes. Leads efforts to integrate continuous improvement within technical programs, driving insights across many workstreams to generate recommendations that deliver operational efficiencies. Facilitates collaboration across multiple teams, driving technical discussions that align priorities and program goals. Provides technical expertise, direction and mentorship to cross-functional teams. Creates and automates reporting, partnering with development teams to continue improving reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models to help manage technical program execution. Acts as a technical liaison with or between stakeholder teams, driving effective collaboration for customer success within Oracle commitments.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Management:

– Leverages technical knowledge to identify risks, manage scope, estimate program timelines, request feasibility, testing requirements, and determine appropriate resources.

– Ensures that product or service delivery meets the third party, security, export, and accessibility compliance requirements.

– Drives rapid response to security escalations, coordinating across teams and communicating to executives to assess risk, determine mitigation strategies, and align and execute optimal proposed path to resolution.

– Forecasts program demands and resourcing to identify risks and ensure that goals are achievable.

– Leads the development and implementation of evolving processes to ensure that organizational SLAs are met.

Technical Management and Execution - Technical Strategy and Execution:

– Utilizes technical knowledge to identify, track, and manage program dependencies and risks.

– Supports rapid response to escalations, coordinating within team and communicating to senior team members to assess risk, determine mitigation strategies, and execute the optimal proposed path to resolution.

– Supports planning by identifying dependencies and risks.

– Develops delivery standards and guidelines in alignment with Oracle best practices.

– Identifies and quantifies opportunities for process automations and advocates for prioritization.

– Contributes to incident management efforts and identifies opportunities to improve processes, as applicable.

Program Oversight - Strategy and Decision-Making:

– Aligns priorities with customers, service, and stakeholder teams through regular reporting to senior leadership.

– Establishes scope and milestones for each program, aligning to the broader program plan and company strategies and goals.

– Assists in defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and measurement methods for program performance against established goals (e.g., scope, timelines, deliverable quality).

– Builds, maintains, and executes a clear communication strategy of objectives to partners and customers, influencing decision-making regarding best practices for Oracle systems.

Program Oversight - Program and Operations Management:

– Manages both technical and non-technical programs and complex, cross-organizational programs impacting products and business.

– Guides the work of program staff (e.g., development, release management, customer success) while providing technical support and direction on removing barriers, including risks and issues in workflows.

– Maintains comprehensive program documentation (e.g., status reports, program plans) and documents risks and issues.

– Ensures attention to detail in program management from planning to execution and reporting.

– Leads regular program status meetings and keeps teams and leadership informed.

– Leads initiatives within the team to improve operational efficiency and enhance adherence to service level agreements (SLAs) and productivity targets.

– Ensures ownership and accountability for forecasting program demands, funding, and resourcing.

– Guides the deployment of change management for programs, such as priority, scope, scheduling, or requirement changes.

Program Oversight - Risk Management:

– Manages highly complex issues, bottlenecks and/or risks, escalating issues when appropriate.

– Conducts comprehensive assessments of costs, benefits, and return on investment (ROI) to inform decision-making and risk mitigation strategies.

– Manages critical issues while making trade-offs between business needs and technical constraints.

– Removes blockers for the program and identifies new technical and resource options to efficiently deliver solutions and drive adoption.

Process Efficiency - Process Optimization:

– Leads program improvement, implementing best practices and driving cross-team process optimizations to improve processes.

– Organizes and develops program objectives and workflows, while testing and deploying cross-functional solutions to address critical business problems.

– Collaborates with management to initiate and maintain processes and procedures that guide and assist teams in reaching their goals.

Process Efficiency - Continuous Improvement:

– Leads efforts to integrate continuous improvement within programs, driving insights across many workstreams to generate recommendations that deliver operational efficiencies.

– Develops and standardizes data-driven decision-making frameworks, ensuring insights drive efficiencies.

– Identifies and addresses gaps to facilitate business-critical improvements to the solution's availability and reliability.

– Iterates processes based on feedback and KPIs, analyzing results through retrospectives.

– Defines requirements and configurations of existing and new development tools, where applicable.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Cross Functional Collaboration:

– Facilitates collaboration across multiple teams, driving discussions that align priorities and program goals.

– Leads medium-scale efforts to optimize processes, identifying and implementing solutions that enhance team efficiency.

– Delivers program updates, risks, and opportunities to managers and leadership, influencing decision-making.

– Develops relationships with key stakeholders, ensuring their perspectives are integrated into program planning and execution.

Collaboration and Program Leadership - Program Leadership:

– Leads programs to continuously improve organizational efficiency.

– Provides technical direction and mentorship to cross-functional teams.

– Influences and guides change at all levels of the group from initiation through delivery.

– Ensures that the program team and other stakeholders are aligned with the program goals and motivated, identifying and addressing conflicts and issues.

Data and Analysis:

– Creates and automates reporting, partnering with development teams to continue improving reports, dashboards, forecasts, and models to help manage program execution.

– Utilizes data to solve moderately complex problems impacting the success of the program(s), including adherence to SLAs.

– Conducts analysis on a small number of data sources with moderate complexity, which may include competitive analysis, trend analysis, and KPI analysis, to drive data-informed decisions to support the program goals, presenting findings with immediate teams stakeholders.

Stakeholder Engagement:

– Acts as a liaison with or between stakeholder teams, driving effective collaboration for customer success within Oracle commitments.

– Manages relationships with internal and external stakeholders to align program priorities and commitments.

– Identifies and documents stakeholder needs and works cross-functionally to implement solutions that enhance satisfaction.

– Identifies risks to customer satisfaction and advocates for improvements or mitigation.

– Assesses risks to customer satisfaction and evaluates mitigation efforts, providing solutions to the immediate team and related teams to ensure alignment on resolving these risks.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

– Manages and coordinates moderately complex tasks, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure timely completion and adherence to requirements for a moderately sized project or initiative. Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.

Collaboration & Partnership:

Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs. Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving:

Continuous Learning:

Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills. Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.

new_jobs.description:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

Design Quality makes sure the design intent signed off in Studio is what customers see and touch in production. As Staff TPM, you will be the cross-functional program lead for Design Quality, integrating DVAC (AAR), CMF and Studio Design Ops activities into one plan, from studio design intent through production release and launch.

You will give Studio, Engineering, Supplier Quality, Purchasing and Manufacturing a single view of schedule, dependencies, decisions and risk. Drive issue closure, report to program and executive leadership, and bring AI into how Design Quality plans, tracks and reports its work.

Responsibilities

Own the integrated Design Quality plan across vehicle programs, linking studio milestones (design reviews, clay and buck builds, virtual reviews, design freeze) to engineering, tooling, build and launch gates.
Plan and drive DVAC (AAR) activities, submissions and approvals for appearance-critical parts, and integrate supplier deliverables and schedules into the program plan
Own Studio program timing: color, material and finish targets, master standards, physical samples and approvals across palettes with different lead times
Partner with Studio Design Ops to sequence studio activities, and translate studio decisions into engineering and supplier commitments and the reverse
Lead Studio and Engineering convergence reviews: present options, trade-offs and recommendations so leadership can make timely decisions
Manage design change: assess schedule, cost and quality impact, and keep changes controlled and visible
Be the issue-resolution champion: drive root cause, mitigation and escalation, and track every issue to closure
Report status, risks and decisions at program gateways and executive reviews
Deliver AI-enabled improvements to DQ workflows as a program deliverable, such as automated status and risk reporting and review-finding analysis, and set standards of work including responsible AI use

Qualifications

8+ years of experience in automotive OEM, Tier 1 or a similar technical field, including 5+ years in technical program management
Experience working in an automotive design studio environment with designers, modelers and studio engineers
Working background in Appearance Approval (AAR) Processes on a vehicle program
Working knowledge of CMF (color, material, finish) specification, validation and approval, including master standards and physical sample management
Technical fluency in vehicle development and the design-to-production process (design freeze, release, tooling, launch) to ask the right questions of engineers and suppliers
Strong program management and execution: able to define the schedule and critical path, control change and adjust priorities as urgent issues arise
Ability to lead through influence, not reporting structure, across Studio, Engineering, Supplier Quality, Purchasing and Manufacturing
Strong written and verbal communication, including presenting options, risks and recommendations to executives and driving decisions
Ability to integrate AI into program delivery as a deliverable: identify use cases, run pilots, measure results and make them repeatable
BA or BS in engineering, design or a related discipline; MS preferred
Hands-on experience applying AI (generative AI, LLM tools, automation or analytics) to program management, quality or design workflows preferred
Jira, Confluence or Smartsheet and dashboard experience preferred
Vehicle launch experience at an EV maker or fast-growing company preferred

Pay Disclosure

The salary range for this role is $154,000- 192,500 for Southern California based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.

We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.

You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than May 25, 2026.

Equal Opportunity

Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.

Candidate Data Privacy and Technology

Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.

Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.

Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.

new_jobs.title: Information Security Analyst
new_jobs.description:
DLA Piper is, at its core, bold, exceptional, collaborative and supportive. Our people are the backbone, heart and soul of our firm. Wherever you are in your professional journey, DLA Piper is a place you can engage in meaningful work and grow your career. Let’s see what we can achieve. Together.

Summary

The Information Security Analyst is primarily responsible for reviewing and analyzing the various security systems we have in place and determining whether further investigation or remediation is required in order to maintain the integrity of the firm’s systems and information. This position plays a critical role in the malware kill chain, acting independently at the prevent, detect and respond levels of information security.

Location

This position can sit in any US office and offers a hybrid work schedule.

Responsibilities

Aligns security alert review and hunting to prescribed Incident Response Playbook.
Conducts limited investigations into security breaches at firm sites using high-fidelity alerts and tools within the environment, MSSP and online.
Reviews alerts generated by security detection tools, correlates with device logs, packets capture and all forms of telemetry; interprets data.
Maintains up-to-date information in alert handling tools.
Where firm SLA governs timing, the analyst must work within the timing bounds to acknowledge and resolve alerts.
Vigilantly protects client and firm data, ensuring proper handling and protection electronically, physically and verbally.
Other duties as assigned.

Skills And Competencies

Must have detailed experience of TCP/IP.
Strong understanding of Windows operating systems.
Experience scripting in PowerShell, Perl, or Python.
Preferred experience includes: experience with Snort or other intrusion detection tools; anomaly detection, full-package capture; centralized logging and monitoring tools such as Splunk; Nessus/Security Center; and experience operating in and complying with ISO 27001:2013.
Understanding a common malware as well as typical attack chain.
Understanding of the common technologies found in enterprise IT environments including datacenter and Internet edge technologies.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.

Education

Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, or related field required.

Certifications

CISSP, SSCP, GCIA or GCIH certification highly preferred.

Years Of Experience

4 years of IT or security experience.

Essential Job Expectations

While the specific job requirements of a DLA Piper position may vary depending upon scope of the job and area of specialty, there are certain universal requirements that are expected of all DLA Piper employees, which include but are not limited to:

Effectively communicate, verbally and in writing, with clients, lawyers, business professionals, and third parties;
