new_jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager,  Recs, Revenue, and Engagement
new_jobs.description:
Our Mission

As humans, there are few things more exciting than meeting someone new. At Tinder, we’re inspired by the challenge of keeping the magic of human connection alive. With tens of millions of users, hundreds of millions of downloads, 2+ billion swipes per day, 20+ million matches per day, and a presence in 190+ countries, our reach is expansive—and rapidly growing.

We work together to solve complex problems. Behind the simplicity of every match, we think deeply about human relationships, behavioral science, network economics, AI and ML, online and real-world safety, cultural nuances, loneliness, love, sex, and more.

Our Values

Take the Lead: We don't ghost our work or each other. Just as users don't leave their matches hanging, we don't let each other down.
Move Fast: We have a bias for action and urgency. Something that could be done tomorrow would be better if done today.
Better Together: We keep connection at the heart of dating and at the heart of how we work. Just as our users are better when they connect with others, so are we when we collaborate.
Real Talk: We say the hard thing the human way. Just as we ask our users to behave with kindness and candor in our community, we expect Team Tinder to do the same.
Safety First: We act with integrity, transparency, and consistency so people feel safe—whether they're swiping, matching, or working alongside us.
Spark Fun: We have fun to unlock creativity, fuel innovation, and help us build better experiences for daters.

The Role

At Tinder, our Recs, Revenue, and Engagement teams play a mission-critical role in shaping the core user experience by helping people "spark something new with someone new" through personalized recommendations, bringing users back at the right moment, and making sure they succeed once they're here.

As Senior TPM, you will drive high-impact, cross-functional programs across these three teams while keeping each team's day-to-day operations running smoothly. You'll partner with Product, Engineering, Design, and Analytics, along with Legal, Finance, Marketing, and Localization, to bring structure to rapidly evolving plans and priorities, resolve dependencies before they become blockers, and deliver incredible user experiences at global scale.

Where You'll Work

This is a hybrid role and requires in-office collaboration three days per week. This position is located in Los Angeles, CA or Palo Alto, CA.

In This Role, You Will

Own end-to-end delivery for high-impact programs across Recs, Revenue, and Engagement from planning through launch, including the ongoing development of recommendation infrastructure and models for Recs; subscription, payments, and ads programs for Revenue; and lifecycle messaging and the CRM platform for Engagement.
Act as the connective tissue between Recs, Revenue, and Engagement and other product teams in the organization, tracking milestones, surfacing cross-team dependencies, driving alignment on ownership and sequencing, and mitigating risk across mobile, backend, ML, and web engineering teams.
Proactively identify and resolve issues by coordinating with teams to determine solutions and prioritize tasks; collaborate with teams as needed to improve existing processes while maintaining a high bar for both quality and velocity.
Provide clear, timely communications to executive and senior leadership on program health, including mission reports, status updates, and escalations that come with a recommended path forward, not just a status.

You'll Need

6+ years of experience in Technical Program Management for consumer mobile products at scale, preferably supporting recommendations, ranking, or personalization; monetization (subscriptions, payments, or ads); or growth and lifecycle messaging.
Proven ability to run a portfolio of concurrent programs across multiple teams, building delivery plans, dependency maps, release plans, and risk registers that stay current as priorities shift.
Demonstrated success in partnering with PMs, engineering leads, and senior leadership, cultivating strong cross-functional relationships and influencing outcomes in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
AI fluency, with hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) to automate routine program management work like status reporting, documentation, and dependency tracking, and to accelerate cross-functional communication.
Expert-level proficiency in Jira and Jira Product Discovery, including configuring views, fields, and workflows, plus Confluence, Google Suite, and Figma.
Expertise in agile methodologies and a deep understanding of PDLC and SDLC best practices.

Nice To Have

Experience with subscription billing and payments, including Apple in-app purchase, Google Play Billing, web checkout, or alternative payment programs in regulated markets.
Working knowledge of the ML project lifecycle, from feature and data readiness through offline training and evaluation to online experimentation and rollout, and how planning for model work differs from planning for feature work.
Experience with programmatic ads, including ad placements, mediation, or SDK integrations on iOS and Android.
Familiarity with lifecycle and CRM messaging platforms (push, SMS, email) and the opt-in and regional compliance requirements that come with them.

As a Full-time Employee, You’ll Enjoy

Flexible Vacation, 10 Sick Days
Time off to volunteer and charitable donations matched up to $15,000 annually
Comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage
100% 401(k) employer match up to 10%, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
100% paid parental leave (including for non-birthing parents) and family forming benefits
Investment in your development: mentorship through our MentorMatch program, access to 6,000+ online courses through Udemy, and an annual $3,000 stipend for your professional development
Investment in your wellness: access to mental health support via Modern Health, paid concierge medical membership, pet insurance, fitness membership subsidy, and commuter subsidy
Free subscription to Tinder Gold

Commitment to Inclusion

At Tinder, we don’t just accept difference, we celebrate it. We strive to build a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of our members around the world, and we value unique perspectives and backgrounds. Even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications, we invite you to apply and show us how your skills could transfer. Tinder is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace where we welcome people of all sexes, gender identities, races, ethnicities, disabilities, and other lived experiences. Learn more here: https://www.lifeattinder.com/dei

If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please speak to your Talent Acquisition Partner directly.

This salary will be subject to a geographic adjustment (according to a specific city and state), if an authorization is granted to work outside of the location listed in this posting.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager (Data), London
new_jobs.description:
Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.

The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery.

Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.

The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you.

About Iso

Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.

Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.

We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.

Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.

Your impact

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM) for Data who is passionate about accelerating drug discovery through the strategic delivery of large-scale, high-quality scientific datasets.

At IsoLabs, you will be an essential member of the Data team, bridging the gap between cutting-edge AI research, Drug Discovery & Medical Research (DDMR), Data Engineering, and an extensive global network of scientific partners and Contract Research Organizations (CROs).

In this role, you will take ownership of the full program lifecycle for critical data generation and acquisition initiatives. You will design delivery frameworks, manage complex scientific and technical dependencies, and optimize the operational speed to deliver transformative datasets.

What You Will Do

Drive the delivery of high-impact data acquisition and experimental data generation programs, ensuring work converges on our core model-training and research milestones.
Partner closely with AI researchers, drug discovery scientists, data curators, data engineers, and legal/commercial teams to define clear program outcomes, governance structures, and delivery roadmaps.

Assured Space Access Technologies, Inc. is a defense and engineering firm delivering phased array, radar, RF payload, and secure communications solutions to government and prime contractor customers. We are headquartered in Irvine, California. This role joins the Ground Based Radar team that designs, builds, and tests the transmit/receive modules at the core of our ground-based phased array radar.

Team:
Engineering, Ground Based Radar (GBR), Transmit/Receive Modules

Reports To:
GBR Technical Program Manager

Location:
Irvine, CA (on-site, with periodic supplier travel)

Employment Type:
Full-Time, Exempt

Base Salary Range:
$145,000 – $185,000 per year

Clearance:
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. An active clearance is preferred.

Position Summary

As the Technical Program Manager for the transmit/receive modules (TRMMs), you will own the plan that takes the module from design through first article and into production. Each module combines a high-power amplifier, low-noise amplifier, core beamforming chip, polarizer, and DC/DC power converter, and it is built from parts and subassemblies that come from several suppliers. You will hold the schedule, the builds, the supplier commitments, and the risk register for that module, and you will make sure the module team, the test stations team, and the radar program are working from the same plan.

You will report to the GBR Technical Program Manager and work daily with the TRMM technical lead, the systems engineer for the module, design engineers, test station engineers, and supply chain. This is a hands-on seat in a small team: you will build and maintain the schedule yourself, run the build and supplier meetings, and know the status of every open part and test lot. Technical depth matters here; you need to understand what the module does well enough to judge which risks are real.

Key Responsibilities

Schedule and Program Control

Build and own the integrated TRMM schedule from design release through first article, qualification, and production transition, tied to the GBR master schedule.
Track engineering, build, and test milestones, report status and earned progress to the GBR TPM, and flag slips early with recovery options.
Manage TRMM scope, configuration baselines, and engineering change impacts with systems engineering and configuration management.
Prepare and run TRMM inputs to program reviews, including design reviews, test readiness reviews, and customer status meetings.

Suppliers, Builds, and Materials

Coordinate with suppliers of module components, subassemblies, and power electronics on delivery schedules, technical status, and corrective actions.
Plan engineering and first article builds: kitting, long-lead parts, build travelers, and build-to-test handoffs with the test stations team.
Work with supply chain and materials operations on purchase orders, expediting, and material shortages.
Support supplier technical meetings, source inspection, and first article inspection with the engineering leads.

Risk and Production Transition

Own the TRMM risk and opportunity register, with clear owners, mitigation plans, and burn-down dates.
Track yield, test failures, and rework from first article builds and drive root cause and corrective action closure.
Lead production readiness planning: build rate, test station capacity, staffing, tooling, and supplier capacity for production quantities.
Coordinate the handoff from engineering builds to production with manufacturing, quality, and test.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, another engineering discipline, or a related technical field.
7+ years of experience in technical program management, hardware program management, or engineering leadership on defense or aerospace hardware programs.
Experience managing an RF, microwave, or electronics hardware product through first article and into production.
Hands-on experience building and maintaining integrated schedules in Microsoft Project, Primavera, Smartsheet, or a similar tool.
Experience managing suppliers and subcontracted hardware, including delivery tracking and corrective action.
Working understanding of RF hardware, transmit/receive modules, or phased array components sufficient to assess technical risk.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship.
Ability to work on site in Irvine, CA and travel to suppliers as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with transmit/receive modules, active electronically scanned arrays, or RF microelectronics programs.
Experience with first article inspection (AS9102), production readiness reviews, and manufacturing transition.
Familiarity with earned value management or formal program controls on government contracts.
PMP or equivalent program management certification.
Active Secret or higher security clearance.
Experience at both a large defense prime and a smaller, fast-moving company.

Medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company matching; and paid time off.
Professional development support, including training and certifications relevant to your field.
Relocation assistance considered case by case.
Hands-on ownership of real scope in a growing defense technology company.

Financial paperwork, agreements, schedules, and records are accurate, current, and ready for review; exceptions are identified early, with a recommended next step.
Practical process improvements reduce recurring errors and delays, and the team can reliably use and maintain them.

You are a hands-on operator. You take as much pride in completing the work as in improving the process.
You bring judgment, discretion, and accountability. You know what you can decide, what needs approval, and how to keep work moving in the meantime.
You improve systems thoughtfully: understand what exists, identify the real problem, and make a practical change without unnecessary complexity.

Operations + Projects: Set and maintain operational priorities with leadership; translate decisions into completed actions; coordinate project handoffs and resolve competing requests within agreed authority.

Contracts + Deals: Prepare deal memos and booking documents from approved templates and confirmed terms; check entity details, dates, and amounts; manage signatures, logistics, and payment milestones. Route material exceptions to leadership or counsel.
Systems + Documentation: Build and maintain the automations and workflows that keep a multi-platform creative studio running.
Founder Support: Keep the decision queue, weekly priorities, and follow-through moving; support schedule and travel as needed.

Evidence that you have personally executed recurring administrative work, resolved nonroutine issues, and implemented process improvements that other people successfully used.
Strong writing, spreadsheet, and document skills, prioritization, and professional discretion. A previous management title is not required; demonstrated ownership is.

Asana, Airtable, Slack, Dropbox, Word/Excel, DocuSign, and designated business-administration tools. Experience with comparable platforms is welcome.

PLUSES

Entertainment, production, talent-representation, or creative-agency experience

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About The Role

As an Implementation Project Manager at 3E, you’ll lead larger, more complex customer implementations where successful delivery requires multiple products, technical contributors, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders to operate against one coordinated plan.

You’ll be accountable for turning the customer’s scope of work into an executable implementation strategy and for determining whether the overall project succeeds—on time, within scope, adopted, and connected to a clear customer outcome. You’ll establish success and acceptance criteria, own the integrated project plan, manage risk and change, coordinate specialists and technical teams, and give both customers and 3E leadership a clear, data-backed view of project health.

You’ll understand the technical delivery deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify dependencies, connect customer needs with the right specialists, and engage credibly with Product and Engineering. You won’t need to personally execute every configuration, migration, or integration; your role is to ensure those pieces come together into a successful customer outcome.

What You’ll Do

Lead complex new-logo, cross-sell, and Value Realization implementations from internal handoff through customer acceptance and formal close.
Translate complex scopes of work into an integrated delivery strategy covering products, workstreams, milestones, resources, dependencies, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria.

Lead customer project governance, including senior stakeholder and sponsor communications.
Maintain the milestone tracker and conduct phase-gate reviews, giving a clear assessment of whether projects are on track, at risk, or behind and establishing mitigation plans when required.
Identify cross-workstream dependencies and risks early and determine their impact on the critical path.
Lead complex, multi-product delivery by managing scope and change control, coordinating custom development through launch, maintaining a unified customer plan across teams, and providing leadership with clear, data-backed reporting on project health, risk, timelines, value, and adoption.
Build and maintain dashboards or reporting tools that make project status and risks visible without relying solely on status meetings.
Lead customer escalations diplomatically while maintaining accountability for customer commitments, decisions, resources, data readiness, and signoffs.
Partner with Commercial on implementation handoff and identify expansion opportunities or renewal risks surfaced during delivery.

About The Role:

We're looking for a Senior Technical Project Manager
to own the end-to-end onboarding and implementation journey for new enterprise customers. You'll sit at the center of every new deployment — orchestrating the work between customers and Laurel's implementation engineers, keeping projects on track, and ensuring every go-live is high quality, not just on time.

This role is for someone who is equally comfortable in a kickoff call with a customer's executive team and a technical deep-dive with an engineer. What You Will Do:

Translate technical concepts — integration architecture, XPATH-based mapping, API behaviors — into clear language for stakeholders at all levels.
Apply agentic AI tools and technology-enabled workflows to scale your own effectiveness and bring creative efficiency to implementation challenges.

What We're Looking For:

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Strategic Management, Management Information Systems, Computer Information Systems, or a related field.

Excellent communicator across all settings: executive briefings, customer calls, written updates, and engineering stand-ups.
PMP, CAPM, or equivalent certification is a plus.

What Laurel is

Laurel is building the system of record for human and agentic work.

The trust Laurel has built with regulated enterprises—and, even more importantly, their end-users— has enabled it to be the first company ever to deploy a multimodal desktop agent at scale (45K+ professionals and 70+ countries). This enables Laurel to collect work that no one else has.

Half of enterprise work happens in systems with no API or OS-level access which no tech—other than a multimodal desktop agent—can capture.

Laurel collects more than just metadata; it captures the work itself. And to make the data useful, Laurel builds workflows that requires the professional who did the work to label it accurately, creating a reinforcement learning flywheel that nobody else in the world has.

The result is +2B (and counting) of human-verified labels, creating what is becoming the world’s largest repository of last-mile enterprise data and workflows.

Laurel developed its data infrastructure by creating the AI Billing category in professional services (legal, accounting, consulting). Laurel earned the trust of the enterprise (in the form of +$1B in profit returned) and end-users (in the form of 1.53M work hours returned) to collect all digital work, even work happening in digital systems that were previously invisible to AI.

Laurel is now re-running the same playbook in financial services (insurance, banks, private equity, etc). Same data infrastructure. But instead of billing, it is creating the Work Observability category to expand its feedback loop.

What’s next

Packaging its last-mile data in the form of:

Post-training: an open-source model on Laurel’s data improved performance by 33%, matching the frontier, at 1% of the cost.
Context: Feeding this data into a frontier model’s context window improves task automation by 21%.
This is how Laurel accelerates its growth from 4x YoY (current) to +10x YoY).

World Wide Technology (WWT) strives to make a new world happen. WWT's work benefits clients and partners as much as it does its people and community across the globe. At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

The Global Learning & Development (GL&D) Measurement Lead drives operational and business-impact measurement capabilities across GL&D by helping teams build meaningful measurement plans and translating data into insights that improve decisions and demonstrate value to the business.

As GL&D evolves from measuring learning activity to demonstrating business value, this role serves as the department's authority on learning effectiveness, business impact, strategic performance, and operational reporting. The Measurement Lead establishes consistent frameworks and standards while helping teams connect learning investments, strategic priorities, and operational performance to measurable outcomes.

This role operates in close partnership with the GL&D Strategy Lead and Strategy Execution and Change Management Lead, as well as HR analytics and reporting teams. Success is measured by the quality, consistency, and use of measurement across GL&D and by the extent to which insights improve decisions, strengthen execution, and demonstrate value to the business.

Key Responsibilities

GL&D Measurement & Performance Reporting

Own the GL&D Success Scorecard, transformation metrics, portfolio health reporting, and Quarterly Business Review measurement packages as the department's single source of truth.
Develop and maintain department measurement frameworks, KPI standards, scorecard templates, definitions, and reporting methodologies that create consistency across GL&D.
Translate performance data into clear executive insights, business stories, and recommendations that support prioritization and decision-making.

Measurement Consulting & Strategic Partnership

Consult with learning teams and program managers to identify success criteria, business metrics data sources, outcome measures, data ownership, measurement plans, review processes, and practical evaluation approaches based on defined business needs.
Partner with the Strategy Lead and Strategy Execution and Change Management Lead to define success measures, benefits-realization plans, baselines, targets, and reporting approaches for strategic priorities and major transformation initiatives.
Partner with learning teams and the strategy team to interpret findings, identify root causes, and recommend actions based on data insights.
Partner with the HR analytics team on business impact analysis projects.
Balance analytical rigor with data availability, decision needs, and practical business constraints to create measurement approaches that teams can execute and sustain.

Reporting Requirements & Measurement Capability

Define user stories, business requirements, measure definitions, acceptance criteria, and reporting needs for dashboards and performance reporting, and partner with HR analytics and reporting teams to execute.
Build measurement capability across GL&D through coaching, office hours, templates, job aids, manager resources, and Learning Consultant development.
Continuously improve measurement practices, standards, tools, and reporting approaches to strengthen GL&D's ability to demonstrate value and impact.

Experience developing measurement strategies, performance frameworks, scorecards, dashboards, or business-impact reporting in a learning, HR, strategy, analytics, or enterprise environment.

Strong analytical and data-literacy skills, including the ability to define meaningful measures, interpret quantitative and qualitative data, identify patterns, and develop evidence-based recommendations.

new_jobs.description:
Purpose and Impact:

Our industry-leading intelligence support program informs decision-makers, from ground force commanders to international partners and national security policymakers. Our employees lead the Intelligence community in providing superior Identity Intelligence and regional threat analysis, and developing innovative data-driven solutions, supporting the customer through intelligence analysis and tradecraft proliferation.

Work Schedule:
5 days per week, 8 hours per day

Essential Responsibilities:

As an Identity Intelligence / Counterintelligence Analyst, you will be responsible for producing all-source Identity Intelligence (I2) analysis and intelligence products in support of global missions and customers. You will apply an understanding of I2 and targeting tradecraft to produce analysis focused on the full range of unique identifying human characteristics and modalities to include, but not limited to, fingerprints, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), iris scans, voiceprints, facial recognition features, and behavior for the purposes of identifying and tracking persons and networks. This includes fusing identity attributes, such as biographical, biological, behavioral, contextual, and reputational information related to individuals and intelligence associated with those attributes, to identify and assess threats of individuals and networks, their capabilities and capacity, centers of gravity, objectives, intent, and potential courses of action.

Work Environment, Physical Demands, and Mental Demands:
Typical office environment with no unusual hazards, constant sitting while using the computer terminal, constant use of sight abilities while reviewing documents, constant use of speech/hearing abilities for communication and constant mental alertness. Must possess planning/organizing skills and must be able to work under deadlines.

Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities):

Possesses an extensive knowledge of applicable databases; ability to compile, analyze and synthesize necessary data to provide an assessment within the scope of the assigned mission and government approved format.
Expertise in and demonstrated ability to apply IC and DoD classification guidelines and procedures.
Extensive experience with I2 analytical tools and databases, including BI2R/I2AR, SOFEX, Palantir, AIDP/Maven, Query Tree, Chrome, Analyst Notebook, Open-Source research, Biometric Automated Toolset (BAT), TIDE, Pulse, QLIX.
Demonstrates mastery of qualitative and quantitative analytic methodologies and pursue developments in academia or other fields that affect tradecraft methodology. Demonstrates ability to define comprehensive, new, or unique research approaches that enable rigorous assessments to address and contribute to high-level tasks.
Demonstrates ability to conduct in-depth analysis of analytic operations and knowledge management issues across organizational and intra-IC boundaries and clearly articulates key findings.
Demonstrates ability to work independently and with minimal to no oversight.
Demonstrated ability to review analytic products for cogent arguments, tradecraft standards, and adequate support for conclusions; routinely tests analytic rigor of analytic products.

TS/SCI

High School Education

14 yrs relevant experience, 10 yrs w/ Bachelor’s Degree

new_jobs.title: Disaster Management & Humanitarian Assistance Research Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Overview

The Disaster Management & Humanitarian Assistance Research Analyst supports the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance (CFE-DM) within the Applied Research and Information Sharing (ARIS) program. This position conducts academic research, analysis, and technical writing focused on disaster management and humanitarian assistance, developing operationally relevant publications that strengthen understanding, coordination, and effectiveness across disaster response and humanitarian assistance missions.

The Research Analyst researches and synthesizes complex information to produce high-quality academic and technical products addressing disaster management capabilities, vulnerabilities, and best practices around the world, with particular emphasis on the Pacific Theater. The position requires strong academic research methodologies, advanced writing and editing capabilities, and the ability to translate research findings into practical recommendations for civil-military coordination and humanitarian assistance operations.

Working with subject matter experts, academic institutions, international organizations, and CFE-DM personnel, the Research Analyst contributes to publications, country studies, case studies, training materials, and other information-sharing products that support the Center's mission.

Responsibilities

Academic Research and Technical Writing

Conduct research, analysis, and synthesis of disaster management data and information to produce accurate, comprehensive publications aligned with client-specific style and content requirements, including international civil-military coordination contexts.
Develop a wide range of disaster management and humanitarian assistance materials, including:
Fact sheets, case studies, best practices, research articles, and research studies.
Disaster management reference country handbooks.
Briefings, presentations, memoranda, information and policy papers, planning documents, and conference materials.
Professional journal publications, situation reports, after-action reports, and time-sensitive requests for information (RFIs).

Apply academic research methodologies to identify, evaluate, and communicate relevant findings.
Translate research findings into operationally relevant information and practical recommendations for disaster management and humanitarian assistance stakeholders.

Case Study Development and Training Support

Design and develop operationally relevant disaster response case studies for use in training modules.
Support civil-military training, exercises, operations, short- and long-term planning, and assessments in alignment with the applicable theater campaign plan through research, information sharing, and the exchange of best practices.

Collaboration, Editing, and Quality Assurance

Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to collect and validate information, verify data integrity, and ensure analytic accuracy.
Facilitate integration of external feedback into documents by reviewing comments, recommending improvements, and ensuring products meet target audience needs.
Edit research products for logical flow, clarity, completeness, grammar, punctuation, and overall content quality.
Coordinate with graphics and design staff to ensure drafts meet final production standards for web and print publication.
Directly support print production and inventory management of information products.

Academic Partnerships, Outreach, and Knowledge Sharing

Support the Academic Partnership Program by cultivating academic partnerships and facilitating information exchange with universities, students and interns, academic partners, international organizations, and related networks.
Update data management and information-sharing plans to support program operations.
Coordinate marketing and outreach activities as needed, including website updates, brochure and report development, social media and newsletter content, and engagement with external institutions.
Provide guidance to students on research papers and edit or revise academic papers to translate findings into practical DMHA recommendations.
Coordinate with CFE staff to ensure students are fully integrated and resourced.
Respond to academic inquiries and curate strategic research topics to provide project options for incoming students.

Stakeholder Engagement, Program Operations, and Events

Liaise with other CFE-DM branches and engage staff with relevant expertise, relationships, or country and subject matter knowledge.
Organize and facilitate events, training sessions, and exercises tied to product development and dissemination.
Prepare and deliver presentations and briefings at CFE academic engagements, workshops, and exercises.
Attend regular CFE-DM and PACOM meetings and maintain an updated task and deliverables dashboard for CFE-DM and ARIS.
Support event setup, unpack boxes of information products, and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Master's degree required. Bachelor's and/or Master's degree in English, Communications, Journalism/Public Affairs, International Studies, Disaster Management, or a related field.
Minimum five years of experience analyzing and synthesizing information, including writing and editing disaster research products.
Strong academic research, writing, and editing capabilities, with the ability to understand and accurately communicate DMHA content in Standard U.S. English.
Experience developing research products and technical publications addressing disaster management, humanitarian assistance, or related subject areas.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present reports, briefings, and presentations.
Ability to prioritize multiple concurrent tasks, manage shifting timelines, and maintain strong time management and delivery discipline.
Advanced Microsoft Word skills, including formatting, editing, and publishing technical reports and similar products.
Ability to take direction while operating independently with a high degree of autonomy, along with strong collaboration skills and respect for diverse perspectives.
Experience developing products that promote civil-military coordination during humanitarian assistance and disaster response missions and training.
Experience with public speaking, facilitation, and presenting to varied audiences.
U.S. citizenship required.
Must be able to obtain a SECRET security clearance. Sponsorship is available.

Preferred Qualifications

Current SECRET security clearance.
Extensive experience working in higher education research environments and applying academic research methodologies.
Demonstrated experience producing technical academic publications, including published articles addressing disaster management, humanitarian assistance, or humanitarian assistance and disaster response (HADR).
Extensive regional expertise in the Pacific Theater and familiarity with its disaster management and humanitarian assistance environment.

P hysical Requirements:
The ideal candidate must at a minimum be able to meet the following physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation:

Ability to perform repetitive motions with the hands, wrists, and fingers.
Ability to engage in and follow audible communications in emergency situations.
Ability to sit for prolonged periods at a desk and working on a computer.

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

Within the Ministry of Education and Childcare , the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Division provides leadership and strategic direction to support the education system in improving outcomes and creating opportunities for Indigenous students in Alberta. The division collaborates with Indigenous Peoples and other educational partners to understand and respond to the unique academic and cultural needs of Indigenous students and works to ensure Alberta Education programs and policies are responsive, culturally relevant and effective. The Research and Analysis unit, within the Partnerships and Research Branch, provides research, policy analysis, coordination and support relating to policy, research and data functions in support of the division and the Ministry's goals and priorities for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students.

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Manager, Research and Analysis, the Policy and Research Analyst provides research, policy analysis, data analysis, coordination and support relating to policy, research and data functions within the First Nations, Métis and Inuit Division and on cross-ministry projects in which the division is participating. The position supports the advancement of the Ministry's goals and priorities for Indigenous education and for First Nations, Métis and Inuit students, including policies and programs, and works with others in the division and the ministry when needed.

In this role, you will focus on the following main responsibilities:

Research and data analysis: Performs research, jurisdictional scans and literature reviews on assigned topics, analysis of qualitative and quantitative data from reports, databases, grant programs to address key questions, identify trends, promising practices and inform recommendations for Indigenous education policy and initiatives in Alberta.
Policy and program support and coordination: Develops briefings, policy documents, tools and resources, prepares responses to Action Requests, proactively identifies policy gaps and opportunities, and supports the coordination of First Nations, Métis and Inuit education initiatives and grants and other projects across the division and across the ministry.
Relationship building and partner collaboration: Builds and maintains authentic relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit governments, communities and education partners, and collaborates to implement programs and initiatives that help support student success.
Cross-ministry collaboration and project support: Liaises and engages with staff in the branch, division, ministry and across government, and manages multiple projects with varying timelines to support high-level decision making within the department.
Data stewardship and governance: Supports effective data stewardship and governance, acting as a steward for First Nations, Métis and Inuit student-related data in collaboration with ministry partners.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

Develop Networks: Maintains close relations with internal and external stakeholders by identifying key relationships, engaging a range of interested parties, and influencing others through effective communication.
Build Collaborative Environments: Facilitates open communication and leverages the skills and knowledge of others, valuing diverse perspectives and supporting respectful conflict resolution.
Systems Thinking: Considers interrelationships and emerging trends to attain goals, analyzing long-term outcomes and anticipating unintended consequences.
Agility: Works effectively in a changing environment, takes initiative to improve work processes, and remains calm and composed in stressful situations.

University graduation in a related field plus 2 years of progressively responsible related experience; or equivalent as described below.

Responsibilities

Direct and manage the day-to-day operations, technical defense capabilities, and personnel of the Information Security department. Exercise full managerial authority over departmental personnel, driving staffing strategy, talent recruitment, coaching, performance evaluation, professional development, succession planning, and accountability for results. Partner with Information Technology to embed Security-by-Design and Zero Trust controls across enterprise systems while applying a risk-based approach to evaluate business initiatives, third-party vendor relationships, and emerging technology/AI integrations. Serve as the operational deputy and designated successor to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), actively participating on the Core Incident Response Team, supporting regulatory examination and audit readiness, and holding full delegated authority to lead departmental operations, personnel, and governance functions in the CISO's absence.

Essential Responsibilities:

Program Governance & CISO Deputization:

Assist the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) in designing, maintaining, and enforcing enterprise Information Security policies, standards, and guidelines aligned with industry frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS Controls, FFIEC).
Serve as operational deputy to the CISO, holding delegated authority to represent the department in IT architecture reviews, change management, and applicable risk and IT committees during the CISO’s absence.

Team Leadership & Security Operations:

Supervise, mentor, and direct daily operations for departmental staff, including Information Security and GRC Analysts.
Oversee real-time security monitoring, ensuring prompt triage, investigation, and escalation of security alerts, anomalous activity, and privileged access events.

Incident Response & Digital Forensics:

Serve as an active core member of the enterprise Incident Response (IR) Team, supporting the CISO in managing security incidents, containment strategies, digital forensics, and root-cause analysis.
Step in as primary Incident Coordinator when the CISO is unavailable.
Coordinate and facilitate recurring tabletop exercises across business and operational units to validate incident readiness.

Cyber-Fraud Fusion & Threat Intelligence:

Actively participate in and support the enterprise Fusion initiative, establishing collaborative workflows, joint threat monitoring, and bi-directional intelligence sharing between Information Security and Fraud Operations.
Oversee the threat intelligence and vulnerability management lifecycle, analyzing cyber-enabled financial fraud tactics, threat actor behaviors, and emerging attack vectors to strengthen preventative controls across banking platforms and digital channels.

Regulatory Examinations & Audit Management:

Serve as an operational coordinator for Internal Audit, external third-party assessors, and banking regulatory examinations (e.g., OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve).
Manage evidence collection, track audit findings and remediation plans, and ensure timely resolution of all internal and external audit commitments.

Vulnerability Lifecycle & Attack Surface Management:

Direct regular vulnerability scans, penetration tests, and attack surface assessments across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud infrastructure, collaborating with IT system owners to prioritize and verify technical remediation.

Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) & AI Governance:

Participate in the enterprise Third-Party Risk Management program, providing guidance and oversight to the department on vendor risk evaluations, SOC reviews, and high-risk security findings.
Participate in the AI Governance Committee to evaluate security risks associated with third-party AI integrations and internal AI/agent solutions in alignment with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

Security Architecture, Cloud & Data Protection:

Direct data protection initiatives (DLP, data discovery/classification, encryption) and cloud security posture assessments across hybrid and cloud environments (e.g., Azure, M365).
Collaborate with IT to enforce Security-by-Design, Threat Modeling, and Least Privilege principles within the change management process and system rollout lifecycle.

Security Tooling Optimization & Administration:

Direct the administration, tuning, and lifecycle management of key defensive tooling, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR), User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA), email security, and Web Application Firewalls (WAF).
Evaluate and pilot emerging defensive technologies to continuously strengthen organizational cyber resilience.

Security Awareness & Culture:

Oversee the enterprise security awareness training and simulated phishing program, analyzing risk trends and deploying targeted education for high-risk roles.

Executive Reporting & Departmental Metrics:

Lead cross-functional cybersecurity initiatives from planning through implementation, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives, regulatory expectations, and risk appetite.
Develop, monitor, and report Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and operational program status to the CISO and risk oversight committees.
Perform other specialized supervisory, threat defense, and risk management duties as assigned by executive leadership.

Ancillary Duties:

As an integral member of the Information Security department, this position is also responsible to provide assistance wherever necessary to help the department and the company in achieving their goals.

Qualifications

Education, Training and Requirements:

Required: Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or equivalent experience.
Certifications: CISSP, CISM, CRISC, or CISA strongly preferred

Skills:

Proven leadership, supervisory, and mentorship capabilities with the ability to manage technical personnel and foster a collaborative team environment.
Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate cybersecurity concepts and risk metrics effectively to technical teams, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
In-depth knowledge of modern enterprise network security, cloud environments, and identity architectures (IAM/PAM, Least Privilege, Zero Trust).
Practical expertise in incident response coordination, digital forensics principles, vulnerability management, and threat intelligence lifecycle management.
Strong working knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS Controls, NIST AI RMF), third-party risk management (TPRM), and financial industry regulatory standards (OCC, FFIEC, GLBA, SOX).

Experience:

7+ years of experience in Information Security and Cybersecurity operations/engineering; OR
8+ years of progressive IT experience with 5+ years dedicated to Information Security, GRC, and Cyber Risk Management.
Proven supervisory/leadership experience managing security staff and programs.
Financial industry experience (familiarity with FFIEC, OCC, FDIC, GLBA, SOX) strongly preferred.
Experience with Cloud Security (Azure/M365), modern IAM/PAM, and emerging risk frameworks (such as AI Governance / NIST AI RMF).
All applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

The Regional Sustainment Framework (RSF) Program Analyst provides logistics planning, operational coordination, and strategic analysis support to the PACOM Logistics and Engineering Directorate (J4) in operationalizing the Regional Sustainment Framework. Assigned to the Multinational Logistics Branch, Plans & Exercise Division (J45), this position focuses on optimizing theater-level maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities, strengthening bilateral and multilateral logistics partnerships, and integrating logistics posture into the broader Theater Campaign Plan (TCP), Theater Posture Plan (TPP), and Theater Security Cooperation Program (TSCP).

The RSF Program Analyst supports theater sustainment resiliency objectives and operates independently with minimal guidance in a dynamic joint environment. The position conducts high-level logistics capability assessments, facilitates partner engagements, drafts bilateral agreements, and integrates regional MRO initiatives into major joint operations, security cooperation activities, and applicable theater defense plans.

Success requires exceptional written and oral communication skills and the ability to collaborate across multi-echelon Joint Logistics Enterprise (JLEnt) organizations and foreign military counterparts.

Responsibilities

Regional Sustainment Framework Implementation and Strategy

Operationalize the Regional Sustainment Framework strategy within the PACOM area of responsibility (AOR).
Identify, assess, and leverage regional, bilateral, and multilateral maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities to build forward-deployed sustainment resilience.
Conduct high-level logistics capability assessments to identify regional sustainment opportunities and requirements.
Integrate regional MRO initiatives into major joint operations, security cooperation activities, and applicable theater defense plans.

Bilateral and Multilateral Engagements

Plan, coordinate, and execute bilateral logistics staff talks, working groups, and forums with regional allies and key partners, including Australia, Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, and Singapore.
Support the drafting, negotiation, and maintenance of bilateral logistics instruments, including Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreements (ACSA), Memoranda of Understanding or Agreement (MOU/MOA), and Implementing Arrangements (IA).
Facilitate partner engagements and information exchange with foreign military counterparts.

Security Cooperation Integration

Align regional sustainment initiatives with the PACOM Theater Security Cooperation Program.
Coordinate logistics capacity-building projects, Excess Defense Articles (EDA) transfers, and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) sustainment to ensure long-term partner-nation interoperability and maintenance self-sufficiency.

Doctrine and Policy Alignment

Ensure regional sustainment plans, bilateral arrangements, and security cooperation activities comply with applicable Department of War Directives and Instructions, Joint Publications, and statutory authorities under Title 10, U.S. Code.
Apply applicable policy and statutory authorities governing theater sustainment, bilateral logistics, and security cooperation activities.

Interagency and Component Coordination

Synchronize RSF and bilateral initiatives across PACOM Service Components, including USARPAC, PACFLT, PACAF, and MARFORPAC.
Coordinate with sub-unified commands, including USFK, USFJ, SOCPAC, and SPACE-PAC.
Coordinate with the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSW(A&S)), Joint Staff J4, and defense agencies, including DLA and DSCA.
Collaborate across multi-echelon Joint Logistics Enterprise organizations and foreign military counterparts.

Executive Reporting and Briefings

Draft high-quality staff products, including Executive Summaries (EXSUMs), Information Papers, Action Memoranda, and Talking Points.
Prepare formal staff packages, action memoranda, bilateral agreements, and background papers.
Deliver executive-level briefings to General and Flag Officers (GO/FO) and foreign defense dignitaries.
Present complex sustainment concepts and recommendations to senior leadership and international defense officials.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
Exceptional written and oral communication skills, including the ability to draft formal staff packages, action memoranda, bilateral agreements, and background papers and present complex sustainment concepts to senior leadership and international defense officials.
Minimum five years of experience operating within a Geographic Combatant Command (GCC) environment, preferably PACOM, or at a sub-unified or Service Component headquarters level.
Demonstrated experience managing bilateral logistics portfolios, participating in bilateral military staff talks, or executing Security Cooperation or Security Assistance programs, such as ACSA, FMS, or Cooperative Logistics Supply Support Arrangements.
Demonstrated understanding of the defense industrial base, product support strategies, depot-level maintenance processes, and global commercial MRO networks.
Proficiency with and ability to apply security cooperation management tools, including Global Theater Security Cooperation Management Information System (G-TSCMIS) / Socium, and logistics databases, including ACSA Global Automated Tracking and Reporting System (AGATRS).
Experience using Tasker Management Systems, including ETMS2, LOGCOP, and AI tools such as Claude and Maven Smart System, as well as other essential information technology systems.
Active SECRET security clearance.
Ability to travel internationally within the PACOM AOR, including Japan, South Korea, Australia, the Philippines, and Singapore, and domestically approximately 6–8 times annually, not to exceed 20%.

TS/SCI eligibility.

new_jobs.description:
The Role

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. The whole-of-nation effort to safely and securely deliver the cutting edge nuclear-powered submarine program will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.

This unique opportunity will see you directly contributing to Australia’s strategic Defence outcomes during an important time in our defence history. The Australian Submarine Agency (ASA) Virginia Program Office (VPO) supports the delivery of critical projects under the Nuclear Powered Submarine Program by providing strategic advice to ensure the compliant acquisition of critical aspects of Australia’s sovereign nuclear powered submarine capability.
The VPO is central to maintain ASA’s relationships with AUKUS Partners through the development and management of Australia’s most critical Foreign Military Sales (FMS) cases and naval nuclear reactor arrangements.

As an APS 6 Project Manager within the Foreign Acquisitions & Export Control Team in the VPO, you will contribute directly to Australia's defence capability outcomes by managing international arrangements, foreign acquisitions, including Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programs, and export control compliance requirements in support of strategic capability delivery.

This role is eligible for an additional remuneration benefit known in ASA as a Building Capability Payment (BCP). This enables ASA to provide a premium, in addition to the base salary otherwise payable under the ASA Enterprise Agreement, for positions in occupational disciplines or classifications that are critical to ASA capability. new_jobs.title: Commercial Loan Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
ECLARO is currently recruiting for Loan Operations Analyst for one of our financial services clients.

This is a great role for someone with 1-5 years' experience and looking to grow their career in finance. This team will be handling complex financing projects for major lending deals in energy, infrastructure, and multi-year construction projects to name a few. We are building processes from the ground up so you're really laying the foundation for something big. It's an amazing learning opportunity with lots of room to grow.

Position Overview

In this role, we will trust you to support our expanding loan origination platform. This role will play a critical part in the implementation and administration of the FIS CLS (formerly) ACBS lending system, ensuring accurate loan booking, data integrity, and operational efficiency across the loan lifecycle. The ideal candidate will have some experience in loan operations, knowledge of syndicated and bilateral loan structures, and a passion for process improvement in a dynamic, growth-oriented environment.

Primary Responsibilities

• Support loan administration processes across multiple credit vehicles.
• Collaborate with Investment Team, Portfolio Management, Treasury and Accounting to support the onboarding, maintenance, and data governance of loan transactions, including syndicated, bilateral, agency, and secondary deals.
• Support the day-to-day operations of credit facilities, including onboarding, drawdowns, rollovers etc.
• Assist in the development and testing of lending platform configurations, workflows, and reporting tools.
• Support quality control checks on loan documentation and system inputs to ensure compliance with credit approvals and regulatory standards
• Identify and escalate operational risks or control gaps.
• Generate and review reports for internal stakeholders and regulatory compliance.

Qualification and Experience (Academic, Professional, Relevant Job Knowledge)

Relevant work experience at one or more of the following types of firms: investment bank, private equity firm, or asset manager
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related field.
• 1-5 years of experience in loan operations or middle office functions.
• Hands-on experience with FIS CLS (Formerly ACBS) or similar loan servicing platforms is highly desirable.
• Basic understanding of loan documentation, credit agreements, and syndicated loan structures. CLO experience is a plus.
• Basic understanding of cash-flow waterfalls, IRR bridges, etc.
• Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with a strong attention to detail.
